So I posted here a month ago asking where people bought tea. I ultimately bought green tea from two Japanese suppliers: Hibiki-An and Maiko. My original plan was to review them both together but Christ, this tea is amazing.

Some notes about me: I've drunk tea my whole life, but most of it has been low-medium quality black. In the last few months, I've gotten into Gong Fu tea brewing and various higher quality loose leaf green teas from tea shops in the area. So when it comes to flavor, complexity, or even the words used to describe tea, I don't know where to start. Just to be clear, I have no relationship with any of these tea companies; I'm just trying to find good tea and tell you what I like.

I bought the Hibiki-An tea and Maiko tea at the same time and the Hibiki-An tea arrived first. Hibiki-An offers free shipping if you order $36 or more. It's decent shipping, I think the mid-grade for international shipping. It got here in about 2.5-3 weeks with the holidays - not too bad. I only purchased the cheap shipping from Maiko because, well, I'm cheap, but it was maybe $10 for a couple bags of tea and a tin of matcha.

For the tea itself: I got the premium grade matcha. It comes in a small plain silver lidded tin. You remove the lid and there's a pop-top. Warning: you're about to inhale matcha as it explodes everywhere. I will not treat it like a can of cat food next time. It smells rich and addictive. The smell fills my head with thoughts of overlooking a field of tea plants waving in the breeze under a clear blue sky. The appearance is bright green and chalky. It is lightly oily, causing the chaulkiness to clump together some.

I prepared the tea per the directions with the tea (using the materials I have). I used two rounded teaspoons of matcha, sifted, then added about 80-90 mL of 80C water. WOW! It was so strong that I diluted it with maybe another 40 mL. I did the usucha preparation, which is the thinner way to make matcha. It is so rich. I didn't realize a drink could have such flavor complexity. The texture is unusual - a little chaulky and dry, but it doesn't turn me off. It is a little bitter, but the main word I have is "rich." Also, this tea really has a kick to it. I quit drinking coffee a while back and switched to almost all green tea and sometimes a black. This is definitely a morning tea for me.

In conclusion, if you've been thinking about importing some tea from Japan but have been on the fence about it, it's totally worth it. This is so superior to the flavor I got at the "quality" tea stores here. It really is a nice treat. And the box is a perfectly sized bed for a cat, so you'll both win. Cheers!
